sources.title: NASA Lessons Learned 1398
sources.notes: A ground test power harness was wired with reversed polarity; the safe-to-mate check was skipped, the board received reverse power and needed rework. Symptom: no power on the protected board, damaged parts. 反接 后板子不上电。

sources.title: NASA Lessons Learned 729
sources.notes: Practice list for avoiding overstress: test every cable with a breakout box before it meets the hardware so reverse polarity or a wrong voltage is caught; verify power is off before a connector is mated. Overstress may only show up later as an early failure (drift).

sources.title: NASA Lessons Learned 53
sources.notes: A misaligned connector mated with the wrong half and two pins touched, shorting a battery; arcing damaged the connector and harness. Connector mismate (连接器误插) with no output from the affected rail.

sources.title: NASA Lessons Learned 386
sources.notes: Blind mating: pins made contact before the connector keys engaged, so a misinsert caused a short. Recommendation in my words: choose connectors whose pins only touch after full key engagement, and dress cables so the wrong mate is impossible.

sources.title: NASA Lessons Learned 431
sources.notes: Two identical connectors placed side by side were swapped during assembly (connector misinsert); one swap overstressed transistors. Symptom: wrong or no output until the cables are swapped back. Fix in my words: label or key connectors, second-person check before power.

sources.title: NASA Lessons Learned 722
sources.notes: Harness design practice: respect the minimum bend radius, support breakouts and clamp the harness so it cannot flex. A harness bent too tightly can crack conductors and give an intermittent open.

sources.title: NASA-STD-8739.3 Soldered Electrical Connections
sources.notes: Workmanship standard for hand soldering. In my words: a cold solder joint (dull joint, poor wetting) is a reject; such joints can crack under vibration and give intermittent contact.

sources.title: NASA-STD-8739.4 Crimping, Interconnecting Cables, Harnesses, and Wiring
sources.notes: Workmanship standard for harnesses. In my words: avoid overstressing and excessive flexing of wires during mating; bend radius limits apply; nicked or broken conductors are rejects and show up as an open or intermittent signal.

sources.title: MSFC-PROC-3260 Repair of Lifted Solder Pads and Conductors on Printed Wiring Boards
sources.notes: A procedure for repairing a lifted pad (焊盘起翘) after rework. In my words: too much heat or force during rework detaches the pad from the laminate; the joint looks soldered but the trace is open.

sources.title: NASA GSFC study on repeated rework of component sites (NTRS 20190031786)
sources.notes: In my words: each rework is a thermal excursion; overheat can degrade the laminate, damage nearby parts and leave a latent thermal failure that shows as parameter drift (参数漂移) later, even when the joint passes visual inspection.

sources.title: NASA NEPP/JPL report: thermal cycle reliability of CCGA and PBGA assemblies
sources.notes: In my words: under thermal cycling, solder joints of area-array packages fatigue; the report watches daisy chains for an open. Thermal cycling grows intermetallic (IMC) layers; a thick IMC layer is brittle. Symptom: intermittent open that appears with temperature.

sources.title: 通用 datasheet 事实：LED 反向电压
sources.notes: Every LED datasheet lists a maximum reverse voltage in the absolute maximum ratings table; an LED fitted reversed simply does not light at normal supply, and exceeding the rating can destroy it. LED 反接 不亮。

sources.title: 通用 datasheet 事实：线性稳压器的热关断
sources.notes: Linear regulator datasheets give a thermal resistance and a thermal shutdown behaviour: dissipation is (Vin - Vout) x I, and when the die overheats the output drops or cycles. Symptom: output drift or dropout under load (过温).

sources.title: 通用 datasheet 事实：电解电容极性
sources.notes: Aluminium electrolytic capacitor datasheets state the part is polarised; reversed polarity is outside the ratings and the part can heat and fail.
